medications.dose: 2.5 mg orally once daily; increase to 5 mg after 2 weeks, then to 10 mg if BP >140/90 mmHg and tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong – review annually and after each dose change
medications.purpose: Control hypertension and reduce cardiovascular risk
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends ACE‑I as first‑line antihypertensive in adults <55 y (non‑Afro‑Caribbean) with target <140/90 mmHg

medications.duration: Lifelong – lipid profile review at 3 months, then annually
medications.purpose: Lower LDL‑C and reduce ASCVD risk in metabolic syndrome
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181 advises statin therapy for patients with QRISK ≥10 % or metabolic‑syndrome components

medications.dose: 500 mg orally once daily with evening meal; increase by 500 mg weekly to a maximum of 1 g twice daily as tolerated
medications.purpose: Improve insulin sensitivity and prevent progression from prediabetes to type 2 diabetes
medications.nice_justification: NICE PH38 recommends metformin for high‑risk prediabetes when lifestyle change alone is insufficient

medications.dose: 1 g orally every 6–8 hours PRN, maximum 3 g per day
medications.purpose: Replace ibuprofen for chronic neck and low‑back pain, avoiding NSAID‑related renal risk
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 advises avoiding NSAIDs in patients with hypertension and reduced renal function; paracetamol is an acceptable alternative

medications.dose: 120 mg orally three times daily with each main meal containing fat
medications.duration: 3 months, then reassess weight and consider continuation
medications.purpose: Adjunct weight‑loss therapy for obesity (BMI ≥ 30) when lifestyle measures alone are insufficient
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181 recommends Orlistat for BMI ≥ 30 kg/m² if diet/exercise have not achieved desired weight loss

interactions_checked.interaction: NSAID can blunt the antihypertensive effect of ACE‑I and increase risk of acute kidney injury
interactions_checked.action: Discontinue ibuprofen; monitor serum creatinine/eGFR and potassium 1–2 weeks after starting ramipril

interactions_checked.interaction: NSAID‑induced renal impairment may precipitate metformin‑associated lactic acidosis
interactions_checked.action: Discontinue ibuprofen; ensure eGFR ≥30 mL/min/1.73 m² before initiating metformin and repeat renal function after 2 weeks

contraindications.reason: Contra‑indicated in hypertension with reduced renal function (creatinine 1.5 mg/dL) and increases cardiovascular and renal risk
contraindications.alternative: Paracetamol 1 g PRN or topical analgesia

Patient age and ethnicity not recorded – ACE‑I chosen as first‑line assuming age <55 and non‑Afro‑Caribbean; if age ≥55 or Afro‑Caribbean, consider amlodipine as alternative or add‑on

treatment_summary: Start ramipril 2.5 mg daily (titrate to 10 mg) and atorvastatin 20 mg nightly for hypertension and ASCVD risk reduction. Initiate metformin 500 mg daily, titrating to 1 g BID, to manage prediabetes. Replace ibuprofen with paracetamol 1 g PRN for pain, eliminating NSAID‑related renal risk. Offer Orlistat 120 mg TDS if weight loss is insufficient after lifestyle intervention. Arrange baseline labs (eGFR, electrolytes, LFTs, lipid panel, QRISK) and monitor renal function, potassium, and lipid response per NICE NG136, CG181, and PH38. Provide non‑pharmacologic advice: diet, exercise, smoking cessation, alcohol moderation, and referral to the NHS Diabetes Prevention Programme.
